gloss: to brace oneself; to prepare for the worst

definitions.gloss: to brace oneself; to steel oneself; to prepare for the worst
definitions.explanation: To mentally prepare and accept whatever outcome may come, resolving not to waver. Implies making a firm decision and facing a difficult or uncertain situation with determination.

examples.japanese: もう{腹|はら}を{括|くく}るしかない。
examples.english: There's nothing to do but brace ourselves.

examples.japanese: {結果|けっか}がどうなろうと{腹|はら}を{括|くく}って{挑|いど}む。
examples.english: No matter what the outcome, I'll steel myself and take on the challenge.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{腹|はら}を{括|くく}って{社長|しゃちょう}に{直接|ちょくせつ}{辞表|じひょう}を{提出|ていしゅつ}した。
examples.english: He steeled himself and submitted his resignation directly to the company president.

notes:
USAGE:
{腹|はら}を{括|くく}る is an idiomatic expression meaning to resolve oneself mentally for a difficult situation. The literal image is of tying up ({括|くく}る) the belly ({腹|はら}), symbolizing inner firmness. It is used when someone decides to stop hesitating and commit to a course of action, accepting whatever consequences may follow.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {腹|はら}を{括|くく}って + verb (to do something with resolve)
- {腹|はら}を{括|くく}るしかない (there's no choice but to brace oneself)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {腹|はら}を{括|くく}る: to steel oneself (firm resolve to accept any outcome)
- {覚悟|かくご}を{決|き}める: to make up one's mind (to accept a serious consequence)
- {腹|はら}を{据|す}える: to gather one's resolve (very similar in meaning)
- {開|ひら}き{直|なお}る: to brazen it out (giving up pretense, sometimes negatively)
